summary: On node1 (RHEL 7.9, no LVM/btrfs/package-repo access available), built a snapshot-capable /srv/data using device-mapper directly: a loopback-backed XFS "origin" volume (dmsetup snapshot-origin target on /dev/loop0) mounted at /srv/data, and a COW loopback store (/dev/loop1). Populated /srv/data with app.conf and state/counter.txt, recorded a SHA-256 baseline, then created a dm-snapshot device (data-snap) capturing that exact state. Modified /srv/data (corrupted app.conf, changed counter.txt, added an unexpected file) to simulate real drift, confirmed the snapshot's COW store had preserved the original blocks, mounted the snapshot read-only, verified its checksums matched the baseline, then restored /srv/data by replacing its contents with the snapshot's exact content — post-restore checksums matched the baseline exactly (extra file removed, originals restored byte-for-byte). Made the setup persistent via a systemd oneshot service (data-origin-setup.service) that reattaches the loop devices and recreates the dm-origin table idempotently, plus a srv-data.mount unit, both enabled at boot. Completed the mandatory single-node restart-evidence protocol: captured boot_id fe422859-bfe7-4eb4-819b-e09864f3ca60 and a healthy/matching-baseline data state pre-restart, issued a background `reboot` so the ack returned before disconnection, polled node1 until reachable, confirmed a new boot_id (4f22c5c7-9866-412e-acfd-70785edf7be2) proving an actual restart, and verified full recovery post-restart: dm-origin device reattached, /srv/data remounted automatically, and SHA-256 checksums still match the original baseline exactly. node1 is the cluster's only managed node, so the restart protocol is complete for the full topology.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 disk/filesystem layout, confirmed XFS-on-raw-partition with no LVM/btrfs and no reachable yum repos
Located device-mapper (dmsetup) already present at /usr/sbin/dmsetup, chose a manual dm-snapshot approach
Created loopback-backed origin.img (512MB) and cow.img (512MB) under /srv/snapstore
Created dm snapshot-origin device 'data-origin' over /dev/loop0, formatted XFS, mounted at /srv/data
Populated /srv/data with app.conf and state/counter.txt; captured SHA-256 baseline
Created dm-snapshot device 'data-snap' (COW target on /dev/loop1) capturing that exact state
Modified /srv/data: corrupted app.conf, changed counter.txt, added unexpected.txt
Confirmed COW store had captured pre-modification blocks (dmsetup status)
Mounted data-snap read-only, verified its content/checksums matched the pre-modification baseline exactly
Restored /srv/data by clearing it and copying the snapshot's exact content back; verified checksums match baseline exactly
Created /usr/local/sbin/setup-data-snapshot.sh plus systemd units data-origin-setup.service and srv-data.mount, enabled them for boot persistence
Captured pre-restart boot_id and confirmed data still matched baseline
Issued a backgrounded reboot on node1 so the exec ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until reachable again, confirmed a new boot_id proving an actual restart
Verified post-restart recovery: dm-origin device present, /srv/data mounted, systemd units active, checksums match baseline exactly

evidence.requirement: Baseline snapshot of /srv/data content and healthy dm-snapshot setup before any modification
evidence.summary: Populated /srv/data (app.conf, state/counter.txt), recorded SHA-256 baseline, then created dm-snapshot device data-snap capturing this exact state (dmsetup status shows allocated COW blocks).
app.conf corrupted, counter.txt changed, and an unexpected.txt file added; dmsetup status confirms COW store had preserved pre-modification blocks (48/1048576 allocated).

evidence.requirement: Snapshot content proven to match the earlier baseline exactly
evidence.summary: Mounted data-snap read-only; its file listing and content matched the original; sha256sum diff against baseline showed 'SNAPSHOT MATCHES BASELINE'.

evidence.requirement: Restore /srv/data to the exact snapshot-captured content
evidence.summary: Cleared /srv/data and copied the snapshot's content back; sha256sum diff against baseline showed 'RESTORE MATCHES BASELINE EXACTLY', with unexpected.txt gone and originals restored.

evidence.requirement: Persistence of snapshot-capable /srv/data setup across reboot (systemd units)
evidence.summary: Created and enabled data-origin-setup.service and srv-data.mount; systemctl status showed both active/enabled with /srv/data correctly mounted on /dev/mapper/data-origin immediately after setup.

evidence.requirement: node1 pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id fe422859-bfe7-4eb4-819b-e09864f3ca60, confirmed dm device present, /srv/data mounted, and data checksums matched baseline exactly pre-restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: Issued a backgrounded 'sleep 2 && reboot' so the exec call acknowledged and returned before the node dropped off the network.

evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed (proof of actual restart, not just elapsed time)
evidence.summary: Node was unreachable during reboot (connection timed out), then came back with a new boot_id 4f22c5c7-9866-412e-acfd-70785edf7be2, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, and a fresh uptime -s timestamp.

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required services and data
evidence.summary: After restart, dm-origin device was recreated (via enabled systemd units, now active), /srv/data was automatically remounted, and SHA-256 checksums of its contents still matched the original baseline exactly.
